 Early voting for the midterm election in North Carolina has seen a large voter turnout compared to past elections.
 On Tuesday, data shows that more than 700,000 people have casted their vote so far in the state. The majority of those voters have been registered Democrats at nearly 45%. Independent and unaffiliated voters make up the second highest amount of votes, while registered republicans have cast the least amount of votes in the state at 21%.
 Democrats are traditionally more inclined to vote early, while Republicans tend to wait until election day.
 Across the nation, more that 12 million ballots have been cast. Voting day for the midterm election is Tuesday, November 3rd.
